title: Western Jin
capsule: The Western Jin dynasty was founded in 265 when Sima Yan (Emperor Wu) deposed the last Cao Wei ruler, and in 280 he completed the reunification of China by conquering the kingdom of Eastern Wu — the first reunification since the fall of Han. The dynasty's unity was short-lived: Emperor Wu's division of the realm among Sima princes triggered the War of the Eight Princes (291–306), a devastating internecine conflict that exhausted the imperial army and opened the north to non-Chinese steppe peoples (the Xiongnu, Jie, Xianbei, Di, and Qiang). The Xiongnu chief Liu Yuan proclaimed himself emperor of Han-Zhao in 304 and his successor Liu Cong sacked and captured the Jin emperors in 311 and 316, ending the Western Jin; the court fled south and reconstituted itself at Jiankang as the Eastern Jin.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Western Jin territorial extent is reconstructed from the Jinshu dynastic history and administrative geography records; the northern frontier is relatively well-attested from commandery lists, though the exact limit of effective control against steppe peoples varies in the literature.
